arguments.content: In opposition to Defendant's Motion to Dismiss (FIL-003), Plaintiff Meridian Technologies Inc. asserts that the complaint satisfies the plausibility standard under Ashcroft v. Iqbal, 556 U.S. 662 (2009), and Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(b)(6). The factual allegations, when accepted as true and viewed in the light most favorable to Plaintiff, establish a facially plausible claim for breach of contract and unjust enrichment. The broad indemnification and non-compete clauses in the underlying agreement (DOC-001) were commercially unreasonable and unenforceable, supporting Plaintiff's claim that Defendant failed to provide adequate consideration. Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court deny the motion in full.

arguments.content: This memo provides an update on matter MAT-2026-0127 (Meridian Technologies Inc. v. Apex Global Solutions LLC). The court docket confirms the case is active in the US District Court, District of Columbia. Defendant's Motion to Dismiss (filed 2024-10-20) is pending, and Plaintiff's opposition has been filed. Key upcoming deadlines include: response to interrogatories (due 2025-01-10), deposition of key witness (2025-01-25), and mediation (2025-02-14). Legal research confirms that under Ashcroft v. Iqbal, a complaint must allege facts sufficient to make the claim plausible on its face. The motion to dismiss standard under Rule 12(b)(6) requires the court to accept all factual allegations as true but dismiss if relief is not plausible. No conflicts of interest exist. All pre-trial deadlines remain on track.
